title: Resilient streaming schema: fallback stubs and idempotent tool-relay semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Clients consuming streamed structured output must be able to make progress even when downstream tool invocations fail or when the network cuts the stream. Current behavior either aborts the emit entirely or leaves consumers with partial, non-actionable payloads. We need a pragmatic contract that ensures predictable consumer behavior, clear retry semantics for function/tool calls, and measurable observability for debugging and economics.

Goals:
- Define a minimal, deterministic start-of-stream stub that gives downstream services enough schema and provenance to act (routing, caching, UI placeholders).
- Specify idempotent tool-relay semantics and tokens so tool calls can be retried safely across disconnects and platform failovers.
- Describe a bounded fallback policy (graceful degradation) that prefers useful partial outputs over silent failures.
- Provide clear acceptance tests, observability signals, and a canary rollout plan.

Non-goals:
- Not addressing large-scale protocol negotiation across different client SDK versions (handled in follow-up).
- Not providing exact cost-optimization heuristics for batching — that remains in Optimize workstream.

Design summary:
1) Start stub: for every streamed request the platform must emit a single well-formed stub JSON as the first record (if streaming is used). The stub contains: request_id, schema_version, model_variant, short_status ("in-progress"), required_output_keys (list), and optional resume_token (opaque string). Consumers can use this stub to allocate UI slots or pre-warm caches.
2) Progressive objects: subsequent items are full or partial records with a 'progress_id' that maps to required_output_keys. Every partial record includes an 'is_final' boolean.
3) Tool-relay semantics: tool invocation requests from the model are emitted as "tool_call" frames with: tool_name, args_hash, idempotency_key (generated by platform if model doesn't supply), submit_timestamp. The platform will accept tool_call frames and return a tool_call_ack (tool_call_id, status: queued). The platform guarantees at-least-once delivery to third-party tool adapters but provides idempotency semantics keyed by idempotency_key to allow exactly-once logical behavior where tools support it.
4) Timeouts & fallbacks: each tool_call has a configurable soft_timeout (recommended default 4s) and hard_deadline (default 30s). On soft_timeout the platform emits a "tool_stub" containing minimal expected response shape (per schema) and a recommendation to retry. On hard_deadline the platform emits a tool_error frame with standardized error_code and optionally a replacement stub depending on fallback policy.
5) Resume & reconciliation: resume_token in stub enables clients to reconnect and request missing progress_ids. Tokens are single-use; platform will accept resume requests up to 24 hours depending on retention policy. Reconciliation includes a delta list describing which progress_ids were completed so client can request only missing parts.
6) Security & audit: every tool_call frame is logged with request_id, tool_name, op_hash and stored in audit logs. Tool payloads marked sensitive must be redacted in standard logs and only appear in encrypted audit stores accessible to compliance roles.

Trade-offs considered:
- Emitting stubs increases token count and latency for tiny requests, but greatly reduces error handling complexity for integrators.
- Idempotency tokens shift some responsibility to model authors; platform can synthesize tokens when absent but will prefer model-generated keys for cross-request deduplication.

Success metrics:
- consumer-visible error rate for streamed structured requests drops by 50% in first month after rollout.
- resume success rate >= 98% for reconnects within 24 hours.
- tool_call duplicate execution rate <= 0.5% for tools that support idempotency; platform-initiated duplicates recorded separately.
acceptance_criteria: A1: First-record stub is emitted for 100% of streaming structured responses within 50ms of connection establishment in canary region.
A2: Each tool_call frame must produce either a tool_call_ack or a tool_error within soft_timeout; soft_timeout behavior must be observable via metric 'tool_call_soft_timeout_rate'.
A3: Resume flow: given a valid resume_token clients can reconnect and obtain a delta list; automated e2e test must validate reassembly of a previously interrupted 12-part stream.

A4: Idempotency: when model supplies the same idempotency_key for repeated tool_calls, the downstream tool adapter must receive the operation at most once logically; integration tests simulate at-least-once delivery and dedup is validated by comparing op_hashes in audit logs.
A5: Fallback stubs: when a tool hard_deadline elapses, the platform emits a validated replacement stub conforming to the recorded schema; schema conformance tests assert shape and required keys.
A6: Observability: traces include request_id and any tool_call_id, and logs surface 'resume_token' issuance and use; dashboards show tool_call_latency_p50/p95, resume_success_rate, stub_emitted_rate.
A7: Security: sensitive tool args are redacted by default in runtime logs; security review sign-off required before rollout to production.
test_plan: Unit: parser/generator tests for stub and tool_call frames ensuring valid JSON and required keys.
Integration: platform <-> tool-adapter harness that injects fail/slow behaviors and validates ack/replay paths.
E2E: client SDK replay test that opens stream, forces disconnect at N=3, reconnects with resume_token and verifies complete reconstruction.
Chaos: simulate platform pod restart during active tool_call and ensure idempotency and resume behavior meet acceptance criteria.
Load: synthetic workload of 10k streaming sessions/hour to verify stub emission rate and latency in canary region.
notes: 2025-02-05: Kickoff meeting — agreed on stub-first contract and default timeouts (soft 4s / hard 30s). Action: ENG to prototype tool_call_ack shape.
2025-02-10: Design review — security requested redaction scheme; added audit store requirement. Action: Security to provide redaction spec by 2025-02-14.
2025-02-16: Opted for platform-synthesized idempotency_key when model does not provide one (decision to reduce integration friction).
2025-02-18: PRD in review; PM requested explicit rollback criteria in case of increased tool duplicate rate post-rollout.
open_questions: Q1: Retention window for resume tokens — default 24h ok for enterprise customers with long-running clients?
Q2: Should platform synthesize idempotency_keys using deterministic hashing across model revision upgrades?
Q3: What is required behavior for clients that don't consume the stub first (legacy SDKs) — do we need compatibility mode?
rollout_plan: Canary: 1% of streaming traffic in us-west-2 for 3 days, monitor resume_success_rate and tool_call_duplicate_executions.
Ramp: 10% for 48 hours if canary metrics within thresholds, then 50% for 72 hours.
Full: 100% after 7 days with weekly check-ins for first month.
Rollback: if tool_call_duplicate_executions > 1% or resume_success_rate < 95% for 4 hours, rollback to previous streaming contract and open incident review.
